architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.tie_interpretation: The deterministic VOI layer is indifferent among the tied top experiments: they share an identical component vector. Tie-breaking is therefore a genuine task left to the Agent, and any selection inside this set cannot have been read off the VOI ranking.
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Run at least two independent preparations with complete process histories. Accept the dual-axis formulation as supporting H-RESIN over H-CORE if the mean SI_15_60 across repeats is below 3.80% and the repeat range is no greater than 2.00 percentage points. The 3.80% limit is half the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction for reactive mass fraction 0.8000.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: Falsify H-RESIN relative to the registered benchmark if the mean SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61% with a repeat range no greater than 2.00 percentage points. Falsify H-CORE if the mean SI_15_60 is below 3.80%. A mean between 3.80% and 7.61%, or a repeat range above 2.00 percentage points, falsifies neither hypothesis because the result is not decisively resolved at the declared 2.00% measurement resolution. This experiment cannot falsify either H-RESIN or H-DUAL against the other because both predict the same low-drift regime for this dual-axis composition.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run an acrylic-only S1C41-derived composition with 15% acrylic-like modifier, zero minor tackifier-like modifier, and the matched reactive mass fraction, using the same M-HOLD-120 protocol, at least two independent preparations, complete process-history controls, and the same 3.80% and 7.61% decision thresholds recalculated for that composition.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured at 120 C over 15-60 minutes
judge_normalized.rationale: This experiment directly measures the declared 120 C viscosity-growth failure mode, tests the dual-axis intervention against the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction, and uses the least burdensome formulation in the stable top set. A low result can reject H-CORE and support formulation-level superlinear suppression, while a high result can reject H-RESIN. The experiment does not establish a molecular mechanism or determine whether the minor tackifier axis is required; the specified acrylic-only follow-up is needed for that attribution.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the proposer and robustness adjudicator in selecting S1C41::M-HOLD-120, breaking the deterministic five-card tie by choosing the lowest supported acrylic loading with the supported 5% minor tackifier level and therefore the smallest justified modifier burden. I followed the skeptic on the important limitation that H-RESIN and H-DUAL remain entangled, and I tightened the repeat-level criterion by requiring a mean result and a maximum 2.00 percentage-point repeat range.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence (thermal-hold drift)
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 formulation increased by 51.54% from 15 to 60 minutes and 93.08% from 15 to 90 minutes at 120 C, compared with 9.51% and 16.85% for E1 over the same windows.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local time-dependent evidence consists of only one original hold run each for E1 and E5, with four time points over 15-90 minutes and no measured modifier-axis series. Thus the magnitude and mechanism of drift across candidate compositions are less resolved than temperature response, which has multiple six-point sweeps, and realized viscosity level, for which E2 has three-run spread data.
measurement_requirements: Measure viscosity at 120 C at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes and report the matched-window SI_15_60 relative change.
Use at least two independent preparation repeats for each tested composition.
Compare compositions at matched reactive mass fraction so the result separates linear dilution from modifier-specific suppression.
Include an acrylic-only composition and a composition with a non-zero minor tackifier axis to distinguish H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL.
Record the full time trajectory and process history without extrapolating beyond the 15-60 minute decision window.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and matched measurement window, does adding an acrylic-like modifier and/or a minor tackifier-like modifier reduce 120 C isothermal viscosity drift beyond the linear reactive-core dilution prediction, and is low drift achievable with acrylic alone or only when the tackifier axis is active?

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 3.80% across at least two independent repeats, the result supports H-RESIN over H-CORE because drift is below half the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction. It also falsifies H-CORE at the stated 2.00% resolution, but does not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL because both predict the same low-drift regime for this dual-axis composition.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result is consistent with the linear-dilution prediction of H-CORE. If SI_15_60 is below 3.80%, H-CORE is falsified; that low-drift result would support resin-specific suppression but still would not identify whether the tackifier axis is required.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result between 3.80% and 7.61% is not a clean separation at the registered criteria: it would weaken the strict superlinear-suppression claim without confirming linear dilution, and could reflect partial suppression, realization-state variability, or insufficient separation relative to the 2.00% measurement resolution. The full 15, 30, 45 and 60 minute trajectory and repeat agreement should be retained for adjudication.

proposer.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured directly at 120 C over the 15-60 minute matched window

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It is deterministically tied and equally interpretable, but uses 17.5% acrylic rather than the minimum supported 15%, increasing modifier burden without adding a registered hypothesis pair.
It is deterministically tied, but uses 20% acrylic and therefore departs farther from the reactive-core anchor without improving discrimination or measurement directness.
It is deterministically tied, but its 22.5% acrylic loading adds intervention burden while providing the same two separable hypothesis pairs.
It is deterministically tied, but uses the largest supported acrylic loading, making it the greatest justified departure from the local reactive core with no additional discrimination.

proposer.reasoning: The declared failure is 120 C hold drift, and the matched-window hold directly measures that coordinate with no model fit or extrapolation. At 15% acrylic plus 5% tackifier, the composition remains inside both externally supported intervention regions, has a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000, and separates H-CORE from both H-RESIN and H-DUAL at the registered resolution. It cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL, so an acrylic-only hold would be required as the follow-up for tackifier-axis attribution. The selection within the real five-card tie is based on minimum supported modifier burden, not card ordering.
proposer.tie_break_justification: S1C41 uses the lowest acrylic loading in the externally supported acrylic region and the repeatedly supported 5% minor-tackifier region, giving the smallest supported total modifier burden while retaining full two-axis coverage. It therefore tests the mechanism with less departure from the characterized reactive core than the other tied cards. The primary observable is the directly measured failure coordinate, not a model-derived quantity.

residual_decision_risk: H-RESIN and H-DUAL remain entangled by the dual-axis composition and cannot be separated by this experiment.
Uncontrolled process state remains a confounder; existing E2 data show substantial realization-state variability at 120 C.
At least two repeats are required but repeat-level disagreement and boundary adjudication are not fully prespecified.
Interpretation depends on the E1-derived linear-dilution benchmark rather than a matched reactive-core control measured in the same batch.
The result supports formulation-level rheological hypotheses only and cannot establish a molecular reaction pathway or axis-specific molecular mechanism.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is valid: S1C41 cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL because both predict the same low-drift regime for the dual-axis composition, and the proposer incorrectly listed that pair as separated. This limits the claims that can be made from the result but does not make the proposed M-HOLD-120 experiment scientifically unsuitable. It directly measures the declared failure coordinate and can still distinguish the linear-dilution H-CORE prediction from suppression relative to that benchmark. An acrylic-only matched composition should be run as a follow-up, with predeclared repeat adjudication and process-history controls, to determine whether the tackifier axis is required.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal is one of the five tied deterministic top experiments. The tied top set has top_experiment_set_stability 1.0, with no flipped scenarios across the 25 re-weightings. Every recommendation_flip_boundary is null, so no tested scaling of decision relevance, extrapolation risk, hypothesis discrimination, measurement interpretability, process state risk, or uncertainty reduction changes the top set. No defensible weight perturbation in the supplied sweep changes the decision, although the base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower is small at 0.004583. Selection of S1C41 within the tie is scientifically defensible because it uses the lowest supported acrylic loading with the supported 5% tackifier level and minimizes modifier burden while retaining the dual-axis intervention.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The criterion is attainable in the narrow sense that SI_15_60 is directly measured over 15-60 minutes at 120 C and the stated boundaries, below 3.80% and at or above 7.61%, are separated by more than the declared 2.00% resolution. However, the protocol must define repeat-level adjudication because only at least two repeats are required and process state is uncontrolled. The criterion can falsify H-CORE or H-RESIN relative to the benchmark, but cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
leakage_findings: No reliance on the target validation formulation identity, target wet-lab outcome, or outcome-derived labels is evident; original E1/E5 data and pre-result analogue evidence are allowed by the supplied evidence policy.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low SI_15_60 result could support suppression relative to H-CORE but cannot support the stronger claim that resin modification generally causes the effect or that the minor tackifier axis is unnecessary.
objections.objection: The selected S1C41 composition contains both 15% acrylic-like modifier and 5% minor tackifier-like modifier. For this composition, H-RESIN and H-DUAL make the identical prediction of 3.804% drift, so the M-HOLD-120 protocol cannot distinguish whether the tackifier axis is required. The proposer admits this in the outcome interpretation and reasoning, but the field hypotheses_separated incorrectly lists H-RESIN and H-DUAL as separated while hypotheses_not_separated lists their pair.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment can test a dual-axis composition against a dilution-only benchmark, but cannot establish the claimed specialization that acrylic primarily changes viscosity level whereas the tackifier is required for drift suppression.
objections.objection: The intervention changes the acrylic-like axis and the minor-tackifier-like axis simultaneously, while also reducing the reactive mass fraction to 0.8000. Although the reactive-mass change is part of the registered dilution comparison, the two modifier axes are not independently varied in this experiment. Therefore the protocol cannot attribute any excess suppression beyond the 7.608% linear-dilution prediction specifically to acrylic chemistry, specifically to the tackifier, or to their interaction.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Intermediate or discordant results could be post hoc classified as realization-state variability rather than producing a decisive falsification, weakening the claimed ability to reject H-CORE or H-RESIN.
objections.objection: The registered decision bands for S1C41 are SI_15_60 below 3.80% for H-CORE falsification and at or above 7.61% for H-RESIN falsification, with a 3.80 percentage-point gap between the low-drift boundary and the linear prediction. The catalog declares a 2.00% resolution threshold, so the bands are nominally separated, but the protocol specifies only at least two independent repeats and does not specify how repeat disagreement is adjudicated. A single repeat near 3.80% or 7.61%, or two materially discordant repeats, cannot be assigned a reproducible falsification status under the stated protocol.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Observed low or high SI_15_60 could be attributed to formulation mechanism without demonstrating that the result is reproducible for the nominal composition.
objections.objection: The measurement catalog marks M-HOLD-120 as not controlling process state, and the selected card reports process_state_risk_detail with base risk 0.75 and six missing process fields. Existing E2 data show a 120 C matched-temperature max/min viscosity ratio of 3.5688 across three preparations. Because the hold protocol only requires two independent preparations and does not specify complete preparation, preconditioning, loading, shear, or instrument-history controls, differences in realization state can be confounded with the modifier effect.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The direct drift observation remains interpretable, but the claim that a result below 3.80% demonstrates modifier-specific superlinear suppression is conditional on the registered dilution model and its E1-derived reference coefficient.
objections.objection: The primary observable SI_15_60 is directly measured from eta_15 and eta_60 in the prescribed 15-60 minute window, with no fit, extrapolation, or imputation. This attack surface largely survives. However, the mechanistic interpretation still depends on the unverified linear-dilution benchmark of 7.608%, not on a directly measured matched reactive-core control in the same experimental batch.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low-drift result could be reported as evidence for the registered phenomenological suppression hypothesis, but not as proof of the proposed molecular explanation or of axis-specific molecular functionality.
objections.objection: The protocol can establish a formulation-level rheological result, but M-HOLD-120 cannot establish a molecular mechanism such as lowered encounter frequency, effective concentration, or tackifier-specific action. The registry explicitly limits claims to formulation-level rheological mechanisms and states that no molecularly resolved pathway is adjudicated.

skeptic.recommended_change: Add an acrylic-only composition at the same 15% acrylic loading and a matched reactive mass fraction, using the same M-HOLD-120 protocol and process-history controls, and predefine repeat adjudication. This comparison is required to separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL and to test whether low drift occurs without the minor tackifier axis.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The dual-axis S1C41 composition makes H-RESIN and H-DUAL observationally identical: both predict 3.804% SI_15_60, so the M-HOLD-120 result cannot determine whether the minor tackifier axis is required. The experiment therefore cannot support the proposed axis-specific mechanism attribution, despite the proposer inconsistently listing all three hypotheses as separated.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

voi_sent_to_model.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi_sent_to_model.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 3.80%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.

measurement_plan.name: matched-window 120 C thermal hold
measurement_plan.protocol: Hold the melt at 120 C. Record viscosity at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min. Report the 15-60 min matched-window relative change. Run at least two independent repeats.
